FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH) REPORT

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient: [redacted name]
Age/Sex: 49 years/Male
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Lymph node tissue
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Clinical History: Lymph node tissue submitted for investigation of suspected lymphoma
Clinical Question: Evaluate for plasmablastic high grade lymphoma; differential diagnosis includes Burkitt lymphoma, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), or B-cell lymphoma with intermediate features

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase FISH analysis performed using the following probe sets:
- Tri-color dual fusion probe for IGH/MYC [t(8;14)] rearrangement
- Dual color break apart probe for BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement
- Tri-color dual fusion probe for IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement

Analysis was performed on interphase nuclei and correlated with CD10 immunostained slide to ensure evaluation of appropriate cell population.

RESULTS

1. IGH/MYC REARRANGEMENT STATUS
Probe: IGH (14q32) SpectrumGreen / MYC (8q24) SpectrumOrange
Result: POSITIVE for IGH/MYC [t(8;14)] rearrangement
Signal Pattern: 1R1G2F (1 red, 1 green, 2 fusion signals)
Cells Analyzed: 200 interphase nuclei
Abnormal Cells: 92% (184/200)

2. BCL6 REARRANGEMENT STATUS
Probe: BCL6 (3q27) Dual Color Break Apart
Result: ABNORMAL signal pattern detected
Signal Pattern: Loss of telomeric probe signal
Cells Analyzed: 200 interphase nuclei
Abnormal Cells: 88% (176/200)

3. IGH/BCL2 REARRANGEMENT STATUS
Probe: IGH (14q32) SpectrumGreen / BCL2 (18q21) SpectrumOrange
Result: NEGATIVE for IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement
Signal Pattern: 2R2G (normal pattern)
Cells Analyzed: 200 interphase nuclei

INTERPRETATION
This lymph node specimen demonstrates:

1. Presence of IGH/MYC [t(8;14)] rearrangement, which is characteristically seen in Burkitt lymphoma but can also occur in other high-grade B-cell lymphomas including:
   - Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
   - Plasmablastic lymphoma
   - High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 and/or BCL6 rearrangements
   - B-cell lymphoma, unclassifiable, with features intermediate between DLBCL and Burkitt lymphoma

2. BCL6 locus abnormality with loss of the telomeric probe signal. This pattern may represent:
   - BCL6 rearrangement with loss of the derivative chromosome
   - Partial deletion of the BCL6 locus
   The clinical significance of this BCL6 abnormality in the context of IGH/MYC rearrangement is unclear and requires correlation with morphologic and immunophenotypic findings.

3. Absence of IGH/BCL2 [t(14;18)] rearrangement, which helps exclude the possibility of "double-hit" lymphoma with concurrent MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.

These findings should be interpreted in conjunction with morphologic features, immunophenotype, and clinical presentation to establish the final diagnosis.

Reported by: [redacted name], Ph.D.
Reviewed by: [redacted name], M.D.
